explanation:
[EFFECT] Higher wind speeds consistently reduce predicted bike rentals, with the effect being near neutral at low winds (roughly 0–7 km/h) and becoming increasingly negative as wind picks up. At the highest observed wind speeds (around 33–57 km/h), the model suppresses demand quite noticeably. The relationship is broadly monotonic — the windier it gets, the more demand is expected to fall.

[IMPORTANCE] Windspeed is the second-least important feature in the model, ranked 8th out of 9 with an importance score of 0.020. Its influence on demand is modest compared to factors like hour of day or temperature.

[RECOMMENDATION] On forecasted high-wind days, operators can anticipate somewhat lower-than-usual rentals and may consider slightly reducing bike availability or staff at exposed stations to avoid underutilisation.
